title: karpenter.sh/do-not-evict stops protecting pods from node deletion
quote: The `karpenter.sh/do-not-evict` annotation no longer blocks node termination when running `kubectl delete node`. This annotation on pods will only block automatic deprovisioning that is considered "voluntary," that is, disruptions that can be avoided. Disruptions that Karpenter deems as "involuntary" and will ignore the `karpenter.sh/do-not-evict` annotation include spot interruption and manual deletion of the node. See Disabling Deprovisioning for more details.
remediation: The annotation now blocks only VOLUNTARY disruption. Pods that relied on it to survive `kubectl delete node`, a spot interruption or a manual node deletion no longer do. For the workloads named here, add a PodDisruptionBudget or accept the eviction — the annotation alone is no longer the guarantee it was.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["karpenter.sh/do-not-evict"] != null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each pod printed relies on an annotation that no longer blocks involuntary disruption

title: Karpenter's controller loses its default resource requests and limits

detection.reason: whether the running resources came from the chart's defaults or from your own values cannot be told apart from the rendered workload — both look like an explicit request

quote: Default resources `requests` and `limits` are removed from the Karpenter's controller deployment through the Helm chart. If you have not set custom resource `requests` or `limits` in your Helm values and are using Karpenter's defaults, you will now need to set these values in your Helm chart deployment.
remediation: Set `resources.requests` and `resources.limits` explicitly in your Helm values before upgrading. If you were relying on the chart's defaults, the controller comes back with none, which on a busy cluster is the difference between a scheduled pod and an evicted one.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("karpenter/controller")) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)"'  # the Karpenter controller workload and the exact version tag it runs -- then read its resources block
